key_insight: Sparse, noisy ocean observations can be used directly to train a generative state-space model, improving reconstruction and prediction beyond dependence on complete reanalysis data.
engineering_relevance: This provides a scalable route for ocean and Earth system models to learn from real-world incomplete measurements, reducing reliance on expensive fully observed training datasets.
method: Use a continuous-state hidden Markov model to represent ocean states and observations.
Implement initial-state and transition dynamics with neural networks; model observations with a masked Gaussian emission.
Train via an EM framework that alternates Langevin-based state reconstruction and neural-network optimization.
evidence_signal: The approach was evaluated on CMIP6 simulation data and FY-3D satellite data, where it achieved high-fidelity reconstruction and accurate prediction from sparse observations.
watch_item: Performance depends on the stationary, ergodic, Markovian assumption and the approximation of optimization with only length-two state sequences.
paper_title: Incomplete Observations Boost Evolutionary Performance in Ocean Modeling
